tools.name: find_facility_types
tools.description: Use this when a user describes a business funding need and wants to know which types of business finance could fit. Takes a description of the business and the need, and returns up to four matching facility types (for example invoice finance, asset based lending, a term loan, bridging or development

tools.name: explain_facility
tools.description: Use this when a user asks how one type of business finance works. Returns a summary, how it works, typical uses, who it suits, what lenders usually look at and indicative terms for the chosen facility type, taken from growthbusinessfinance.com. General information, not advice.

tools.name: estimate_size
tools.description: Use this when a user wants a rough idea of how much a facility type could raise against a figure they know, such as their debtor book, stock value, asset cost, property value or EBITDA. tools.name: example_deals
tools.description: Use this when a user asks for examples of business finance deals. Returns up to three anonymous, published stories of completed deals that Growth Business Finance arranged, optionally filtered by facility type or sector. They are a selection, with no client or lender names.

tools.name: submit_enquiry
tools.description: Use this only when the user asks to send an enquiry to Growth Business Finance, a UK commercial finance broker. It sends the user's business, funding need and contact details to GBF, where a human broker reviews it, and returns a reference and the next steps. Before calling: show the user a summary

tools.name: get_available_slots
tools.description: Use this after submit_enquiry returns a booking_token and the user wants to book a call with Growth Business Finance. Returns up to six free 30 minute slots from the broker's calendar over the next two weeks, in the user's time zone and in UK time. It only reads availability and books nothing. Witho

tools.name: book_call
tools.description: Use this only when the user has chosen one of the slots from get_available_slots and asked to book it. findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "submit_enquiry" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: submit_enquiry, get_available_slots, book_call · Private data: find_facility_types, submit_enquiry · Public sink: submit_enquiry, get_available_slots, book_call.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: submit_enquiry, get_available_slots, book_call · Private data: find_facility_types, submit_enquiry · Public sink: submit_enquiry, get_available_slots, book_call

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
